title: Iran Blockade Capability Assessed as Weakening; Hormuz Crude Exports Recover to ~80% of Pre-Crisis Levels
detail: Iran's ability to sustain its Strait of Hormuz blockade was assessed as weakening on September 29, with Middle East crude exports recovering to approximately 80% of pre-conflict levels — up from the ~72% baseline reported as recently as September 28. The incremental rebound reflects continued US Navy passage-protection operations and growing pressure on Iran's interdiction resources, which US officials have characterised as increasingly 'exhausted.' The 80% recovery mark, if sustained, would represent the highest export restoration since the onset of the crisis.

title: Oil Shipments Through Hormuz Rise to Almost Pre-War Levels Ahead of Formal Reopening
detail: Oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz rose to almost pre-war levels on September 29, 2026, ahead of announced plans to formally reopen the strait — a further recovery milestone in Persian Gulf energy flows. The near-full restoration of crude throughput marks a significant reversal from the acute disruptions at the crisis peak, signalling that passage-protection operations and diplomatic pressure have substantially restored commercial shipping confidence through the waterway.

title: Mideast Oil Exports Rebounding as Crude Prices Remain Elevated Despite Partial Volume Recovery
detail: Middle East oil exports continued rebounding on September 29, 2026, even as regional crude prices remained elevated despite the partial recovery in export volumes. A New York Times analysis confirmed continued market tension, noting that while export throughput has partially recovered from crisis lows, supply uncertainty and risk premiums embedded in crude pricing have not yet normalised. The divergence between recovering volumes and persistently elevated prices reflects lingering shipper caution and demand-side uncertainty in downstream markets.
